jobs.description:
OUR COMPANY

Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

Tasks & responsibilities

- In this role, you will leverage your extensive legal expertise to mitigate launch risks from third party patents for our newly developed products as well as to enforce and defend our patents to defend our products against patent infringement.
- With a strategic mindset, you will develop complex launch risk mitigation strategies in a cross functional set up and provide tailored advice to the business how to leverage upside potential from our existing patent portfolios.
- Managing and instructing our network of external lawyers and patent attorneys in disputes including in-court infringement and nullity proceedings will be a key part of your responsibilities.
- In addition, you will support the negotiation and drafting of complex agreements to find the best possible solutions for Boehringer Ingelheim.

Requirements

- Fully qualified lawyer, preferably with honors in the second state examination. An additional qualification (LL.M. or comparable degree with a focus on IP law) is desirable
- Longterm specialization in the field of intellectual property and the pharmaceutical industry at an international level as well as extensive experience in managing large international IP portfolios
- Longterm relevant professional experience in external law firms specialized on patent litigation or in a comparable in-house position as a corporate counsel
- Experience in leading, coordinating, and managing patent litigation
- Knowledge and experience in the pharmaceutical industry
- Strong strategic understanding and the ability to quickly grasp and clearly present legally and technically complex matters
- High level of teamwork and excellent communication skills in English and German

What we offer

With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.

Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.

Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.

Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

HOW TO REACH US

- Bekim Krasniqi (Talent Acquisition), bekim.krasniqi@basf.com, Tel.:+49 30 2005-56136 will be happy to answer your questions for this position. You are also welcome to book an appointment online. Technical questions cannot be answered at this meeting.

WELCOME
If you're someone who inspires others, owns their impact and wants to elevate what they do, you'll fit right in.
Until July 1, our business was part of BASF. As part of the current transition, all job listings and the application process are still hosted on the BASF platform and therefore fully presented in BASF branding.
Please do not be confused by this: All roles are positions at Surventis, and your application will be submitted to us.
At Surventis, we go beyond the surface - in everything we do. We put customers at the center, think one step ahead, and develop solutions that create real value and lasting partnerships.
We inspire each other to think further, take ownership of our work, and constantly push to elevate what's possible. If you bring your full self, challenge the obvious answer, and want to grow with a team that means it - this is your place

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT
Due to the strategic realignment of the Coatings business unit, a dedicated accounting department is being established. This presents an exciting opportunity to develop and shape the finance organization from its foundation. Therefore, we are looking for a Global Functional Process Owner Book-to-Report / Record-to-Report (B2R) | Asset and Project Accounting with the following objectives:

- You own the global B2R | Asset- and Project Accounting Finance processes, which include the project accounting lifecycle from the initial financial evaluation until the execution of the financial project start-up and project closure, as well as asset accounting processes and lease accounting according to IFRS 16.
- You establish and maintain global standards for B2R | Asset- and Project Accounting processes, ensuring these are aligned with organizational goals and regulatory requirements across the coatings division.
- Moreover, you oversee the asset and project accounting activities, identify and drive process improvement opportunities, leveraging technology and digital solutions to enhance automation, efficiency, and continuous improvement within the finance organization.
- Furthermore, you manage a third-party business process provider in the area of Asset- and Project Accounting and implement process performance KPIs to steer the service provider.
- You collaborate closely with related functions such as project engineering, Purchase-to-Pay and General Ledger Accounting, you coordinate integration efforts and ensure holistic alignment of accounting processes.
- In addition, you engage with internal stakeholders to ensure that Asset- and Project Accounting processes meet business needs and support strategic objectives.

WHAT YOU OFFER

- university degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field; additional certifications such as CMA or CPA are an advantage
- at least 10 years of work experience in financial process management and optimization, with a strong focus on Asset- and Project Accounting activities in a multinational corporation
- experience in the chemicals industry or a related industry, particularly during transitions or carve-outs, is highly beneficial
- strong understanding of accounting processes and process optimization methodologies
- proficiency in SAP R/3 and S/4, process mapping tools, and advanced MS Office skills
- excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage and influence diverse stakeholders in a multicultural environment
- fluency in English is required

WHAT WE OFFER

- We offer an attractive salary with individual benefits such as performance-related bonuses. Company-funded supplementary health insurance, accident insurance and pension related benefits.
- We offer a wide range of local and global development and career opportunities for professional and personal development.
- Surventis stands for diversity - we are proud of our Coatings employee networks WomenInCoatings, Color Pride and CultiConnect.
- The feedback culture is firmly integrated into our corporate culture, e.g. through regular employee surveys and management feedback.
- At our location in Münster, we have our own fitness studio "Freizeit" with a physiotherapy practice, permanently employed company doctors, a company restaurant "Auszeit" including a café bar, a bilingual company daycare center "LackiKids" and a vacation program "LackiKids on Tour".

Doctoral Position: Gene Expression Regulation (f/m/x)

Uhlirova Lab | Institute for Genetics | CECAD

We are one of the largest and oldest universities in Europe and one of the most important employers in our region. Our broad range of subjects, the dynamic development of our main research areas and our central location in Cologne make us attractive for students and researchers from around the world. We offer a wide range of career opportunities in science, technology, and administration.

The Uhlirova lab (www.uni-koeln.de/inter-fak/cecad/uhlirova/) explores how stress-inducible signaling pathways control gene expression and influence tissue homeostasis and longevity. To tackle these questions, we combine the power of functional genetics in Drosophila and mouse models with cutting-edge molecular and cell biology, multi-omics approaches, advanced microscopy, and bioinformatics. We are looking for a highly motivated and curious doctoral candidate (f/m/x) to join our dynamic team. You will have the opportunity to lead your own project, contribute to collaborative research, and develop skills at the interface of genetics, molecular and cell biology, and systems-level analysis.

The University of Cologne promotes equal opportunities and diversity. Women will be considered preferentially in accordance with the Equal Opportunities Act of North Rhine-Westphalia (Landesgleichstellungsgesetz - LGG NRW). We also expressly welcome applications from all suitable candidates regardless of their gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, disability, age, personal orientation and identity.

The position is available from immediately on a part-time basis (25,89 hours per week).The position is to be filled for three years. If the applicant meets the relevant wage requirements and personal qualifications, the salary is based on remuneration group 13 TV-L of the pay scale for the German public sector.

Please apply online without a photo with proof of the required
qualifications and the following documents:

A cover letter describing your motivation to join our research group and information on your career achievements (1 page max.)
Academic Curriculum Vitae, including your publication list and contact information for three references
Copies of your degree and qualification certificate

The reference number is Wiss2608-13. The application deadline is 27 September 2026.
For further inquiries, please contact Dr Esther Wollert (uhlirova-jobs@uni-koeln.de) and take a look at our FAQs. YOUR TASKS

To study the crosstalk between transcription and pre-mRNA splicing under physiological, stress, and disease conditions
To investigate mechanisms underlying spliceosome assembly and functional plasticity
To uncover what renders different transcripts, cells, and tissues sensitive to aberrant splicing
To investigate how spliceosome malfunction contributes to loss of tissue homeostasis, premature aging and diseases

Completed Master‘s degree or equivalent in Biology / Biochemistry/ Biophysics or related areas of Life Sciences
Strong background in genetics, molecular and cell biology is essential
Motivation, curiosity and creativity, and a strong ability to solve problems through critical analytical thinking
Proven ability to carry out an independent scientific project and unwavering commitment to high quality research
Hands-on experience in working with model organisms, preferably Drosophila and/or mouse and cell culture systems

The Friedrich Schiller University Jena is a dynamic and innovation-driven university centrally located in Germany. With a broad range of disciplines, it shapes the future through excellent research and teaching. Its scientific excellence is reflected in the profile areas Light - Life - Liberty, which provide pioneering insights and sustainable solutions for the society of tomorrow. The Institute of Biodiversity, Ecology and Evolution at the Faculty of Biological Sciences seeks to fill the position of a

Doctoral Researcher in Viral Ecology (m/f/d)

commencing on 01 December 2026. We offer a part-time position (65%, 26 hours per week), with a fixed-term employment until 30 June 2030.

The DFG-funded Collaborative Research Centre 1768 “VirusREvolution: Decoding tools for virus research” is a highly ambitious research centre at Friedrich Schiller University with the joint goal to develop novel tools for virus discovery, characterisation, regulation, interaction, and visualisation (https://virusrevolution.uni-jena.de/). Its integrated research training group is educating doctoral researchers in a structured, interdisciplinary training program and invites applications for doctoral and postdoctoral researcher positions in various fields of research.
In this doctoral project “Do viruses exploit their quasispecies for host range evolution?”, you will investigate how host range and environmental conditions shape virus diversity and virus-host interactions in natural and experimentally manipulated microbial communities.
Conduct experimental work and analyses on virus-host interactions in soil and groundwater ecosystems, including host-range assays, environmental sampling, and targeted microcosm experiments
Analyse metagenomic and viromic data sets from soil and groundwater samples to identify broad- and narrow-host-range viruses to characterize their quasispecies characteristics
Participation in the Collaborative Research Centre VirusREvolution and close collaboration with the tandem project partner

Publish papers and present your work at national and international scientific meetings

Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving
Ability to work independently and in a collaborative team

jobs.description:
At Bayer we’re visionaries, driven to solve the world’s toughest challenges and striving for a world where ,Health for all, Hunger for none’ is no longer a dream, but a real possibility. We’re doing it with energy, curiosity and sheer dedication, always learning from unique perspectives of those around us, expanding our thinking, growing our capabilities and redefining ‘impossible’. There are so many reasons to join us. If you’re hungry to build a varied and meaningful career in a community of brilliant and diverse minds to make a real difference, there’s only one choice.

Senior Principal Scientist (all genders) - Quantum Mechanics and Modeling

As a key player in our R&D digital transformation, you will leverage quantum mechanics, physics-based modeling, machine learning and AI to predict molecular properties, design and prioritize compounds across our discovery portfolio. Collaborating closely with medicinal chemists, structural biologists, biologists, and data engineers, you will drive discovery project milestones and advance our digital transformation in R&D. Your role is crucial in shaping the future of drug discovery and development through innovative digital solutions.

YOUR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

- You advance drug discovery projects using quantum mechanics, data science, and modeling approaches to enable data‑driven decision‑making.
- You enable AI‑augmented Design‑Make‑Test‑Analyze cycles by advancing and applying methods for in‑silico compound design and characterization.
- 
Applying cutting‑edge quantum mechanics methods to advance drug development and to generate a deep understanding of molecular interactions is central to your function

- You collaborate closely with experimentalists and internal partners to identify scientific challenges and develop effective solutions.
- You lead strategic digital initiatives and actively co‑shape the R&D digital strategy.
- Working closely with the Data Science & AI unit to leverage next‑generation technologies and drive the adoption of digital solutions is a core part of your role
- You share your skills and knowledge by coaching and teaching others, demonstrating collaborative and supportive behaviors.
- You contribute to self‑directed teams that work collaboratively and align with Bayer’s leadership standards.

WHO YOU ARE

- You hold a PhD in quantum chemistry, computational chemistry, chemistry, computer science, or a related discipline, with strong knowledge of organic chemistry.
- Demonstrated success in an industry setting defines your professional track record, supported by extensive professional experience where you have utilized a diverse range of ligand‑ and structure‑based approaches, including virtual screening, docking, molecular dynamics, binding‑affinity calculations, generative design approaches, and holistic workflows
- You are proficient in quantum mechanics software such as ORCA and xTB, and you have experience in scripting, programming, and workflow automation
- You have experience working with AI‑driven DMTA loops in a pharmaceutical setting, as well as practical exposure to computational workflows that integrate AI, modeling, and chemistry
- You demonstrate high interest in managing high‑performance infrastructure and working with external IT providers
- You emb  holistic health principles and align your work with the organization’s vision as part of Bayer.
- Curiosity, creativity, and a strong passion for drug discovery are central characteristics that define you
- Fluency in English (written and spoken), with strong communication skills and the ability to present complex data clearly and effectively, round off your profile

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

This position can be filled on a full-time or near full-time (min. 80%) basis.

WHAT WE OFFER

Our benefits package is flexible, appreciative, and tailored to your lifestyle, because: What matters to you, matters to us!

- We ensure your financial stability with a competitive salary between 109.800€ and 138.500€ per year (full-time) plus a variable component and a global equity-based cash plan. Your compensation is based on your qualifications, skills, and professional experience.
- Whether it’s hybrid work models or part-time arrangements: Whenever it is possible, you will have the flexibility to work how, when and where it is best for you.
- Your family is a top priority. We offer loving company daycare centers at multiple locations, support in finding childcare, time off for the care of elderly or dependent family members, summer camps for children, and much more.
- We support your professional growth by providing access to learning and development opportunities, training programs through the Bayer Learning Academy, development dialogues, as well as coaching and mentoring programs.
- We promote health awareness and opportunities for selfcare through various measures, such as free health checks with the company doctor.
- We emb  diversity by providing an inclusive work environment in which you are welcomed, supported, and encouraged to bring your whole self to work.

The Medical Faculty of Leipzig University, with its tradition spanning more than 600 years, is one of the largest research institutions in the Leipzig region. With over 1,300 employees, it is the largest of the university's 14 faculties and serves as a training center for approximately 3,500 students in human medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and midwifery.

We are seeking a highly motivated Epidemiologist to design and conduct epidemiological research in pediatric populations, focusing on the determinants of child health, the development of common childhood diseases, particularly obesity, and the prevention and long-term outcomes of childhood obesity and metabolic diseases.
The research group "Childhood Obesity and Metabolic Research", led by Antje Körner, investigates the development, mechanisms and health consequences of childhood obesity. The translational approach combines experimental research, clinical studies and genetic approaches. Our international and interdisciplinary team is closely integrated with the research structures of the Medical Faculty of Leipzig University, Helmholtz Munich, and leading local as well as national research consortia, such as the Excellence cluster LeiCeM, the German Center for Child and Youth Health (DZKJ), and our large children's and adolescents' cohort LIFE Child.
We have large, well-characterized cohorts up and running with a longitudinal setting and across the entire age range: LIFE Child (n~6000), Leipzig Obesity Childhood Cohort (n~2500), and Leipzig Adipose Tissue Childhood cohort (n~700), with deep phenotyping allowing for combining clinical, epidemiological, lifestyle and functional omics and multi-omics data.
Key Responsibilities

- Design, plan, and conduct epidemiological research projects, including cohort and intervention studies.
- Develop study protocols and statistical analysis plans.
- Analyze and interpret complex population-based, clinical, and/or health-related datasets.
- Preparation of scientific manuscripts, reports, presentations, and grant applications.
- Ensure high standards of data quality, reproducibility, and compliance with ethical and data protection regulations.
- Present research findings at national and international conferences and scientific meetings.
- Provide methodological expertise and consultation to ongoing research projects; collaborate closely with clinicians, statisticians, bioinformaticians, and other researchers
- Supervision junior researchers or students.

- Experience in the design and implementation of epidemiological studies, large cohort studies.
- Experience working with large-scale health, clinical, or population-based datasets.
- Strong understanding of epidemiological study designs and methodologies.
- Experience with observational and interventional research.
- Experience in data cleaning, validation, and quality assurance.
- Familiarity with evidence-based medicine and public health principles.
- Track record of scientific publications in peer-reviewed journals is desirable.
- Experience in interdisciplinary and collaborative research environments.
- Knowledge of research ethics and data protection requirements.
- Experience in grant writing is an advantage.
- Knowledge of causal inference methods (e.g., Target Trial Emulation, Mendelian Randomization) is desirable.

Statistical and Analytical Skills

- Proficiency in at least one statistical programming language such as: R, SAS, Stata, Python.
- Experience with general statistical methods:
- Regression modeling
- Longitudinal data analysis
- Missing data methods
- Sensitivity analyses
- Knowledge of modern analytical approaches, including machine learning methods, is an advantage.

Personal Competencies

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent organizational and project management abilities.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams.
- Communication skills: English - excellent; German - very good

- Cohort studies
- Precision medicine and risk prediction modeling
- Multi-omics, biomarker, or biobank data integration
- Obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or metabolic health research

The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that links basic and clinical sciences to improve prevention, diagnosis and therapy of Diabetes mellitus and its complications.

doctoral researchers (65% TV-L E13)

This is a three-year fixed-term training position in accordance with the German Act on Fixed-Term Academic Contracts (WissZeitVG, pursuant to Section §2(1)).

About the CRC 1774
The CRC 1774 investigates how key metabolic “promoter organs”-adipose tissue, bone marrow, the gut, and the liver-communicate with the cardiovascular system and thereby influence the progression from health through prediabetes and type 2 diabetes to cardiovascular diseases. By combining comprehensively characterized patient cohorts with state-of-the-art multi-omics technologies, innovative imaging techniques, and methods from data science and artificial intelligence, the project aims to decipher the mechanisms underlying cardiometabolic diseases and develop new approaches for precision medicine at the interface of diabetology and cardiology.

Doctoral students work on interdisciplinary research projects spanning basic, translational, and clinical research. The focus is on organ-to-organ communication, metabolic regulation, inflammatory processes, cellular energy metabolism, and cardiovascular complications of diabetes within a highly collaborative and international research environment.
